question: England paid hospital nurses the same national rates everywhere. Where private wages nearby were high, what happened to heart-attack patients?
answer: More of them died. Where other local jobs paid well, hospitals bound by national pay scales struggled to hire and keep nurses, and leaned on temporary staff. Propper and Van Reenen found a 10% higher outside wage went with 4% to 8% more deaths after heart attacks. A uniform wage is not a uniform job.
move: A wage is judged against what else the worker could earn nearby.
ask: If someone offered me more for similar work down the road, what would keep me where I am?
trap: Assuming equal pay means hospitals everywhere get the same staff.
reference: Propper & Van Reenen, Can Pay Regulation Kill? Panel Data Evidence on the Effect of Labor Markets on Hospital Performance, Journal of Political Economy, 2010
